q: Consider the following statements about contributions under the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS): I. The employee contributes 10%. II. The Government makes a matching contribution of 10%. III. The Government pool contribution is 10%. Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: The employee and the Government matching contributions are 10% each, but the Government pool contribution is 8.5%, not 10%. Hence only I and II are correct.

q: A UPS subscriber completes 25 years of qualifying service. The average basic pay of his last 12 months is Rs 80,000. What is his monthly assured payout?
e: After 25 years the full assured payout is 50% of the average basic pay of the last 12 months.

q: With effect from which date did the Unified Pension Scheme become operational?
e: UPS became operational from 1 April 2025 as an assured-payout option inside NPS, vide RBE 25/2025. The date 30 November 2025 is the option cut-off, not the operational date.

q: A railway employee retired on 30 June 2025. After retirement he availed and received benefits under NPS. He now seeks to migrate to UPS. What is the correct position?

options.A: He can migrate if he refunds the NPS benefits with interest
options.B: He can migrate only to the Old Pension Scheme
options.C: He can migrate at any time because he retired after 1 April 2025
options.D: He cannot migrate to UPS because he has already availed NPS benefits after retiring on or after 1 April 2025

e: As per the clarification reproduced in RBE 48/2026, a subscriber who retired on or after 1 April 2025 and has already availed NPS benefits cannot then migrate to UPS.

q: Assertion (A): A UPS subscriber with 10 years of qualifying service is covered by a minimum assured payout of Rs 10,000 per month. Reason (R): The minimum assured payout under UPS is Rs 15,000 per month after 15 years of service.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
options.C: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
options.D: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true

e: The minimum assured payout is Rs 10,000 per month after 10 years, so the Assertion is true and the Reason, which states a different amount and period, is false.

q: Consider the following statements about the introduction of UPS: I. UPS became operational from 1 April 2025. II. UPS was introduced vide Railway Board RBE No. 25/2025. III. UPS was set up as a separate scheme wholly outside the NPS architecture. Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: UPS is an option inside the NPS architecture, not a scheme outside it. Statements I and II are correct; III is wrong.

q: For a UPS subscriber, the basic pay taken for working out monthly contributions is Rs 60,000. What is the total monthly Government contribution, comprising the matching contribution and the pool contribution?
e: Government pays a matching 10% plus a pool contribution of 8.5%, i.e. 18.5% in total.

q: Which one of the following statements about UPS is NOT correct?

options.A: UPS restores the Old Pension Scheme for railway employees
options.B: The employee contribution under UPS is 10%
options.C: The Government pool contribution under UPS is 8.5%
options.D: Full assured payout is payable after 25 years of qualifying service

e: UPS is an assured-payout option inside NPS; it does not restore the Old Pension Scheme. The other three statements are correct.

q: An NPS-covered railway employee who is still in service submits his option for UPS on 15 November 2025. How should the office treat the option in relation to the prescribed cut-off?

options.A: It was exercised within the cut-off date of 30 November 2025
options.B: It is late because the cut-off was 31 March 2025
options.C: It is invalid because serving employees cannot opt for UPS
options.D: It can be accepted only if he first exits NPS and joins SRPF

e: The cut-off for exercising the UPS option was 30 November 2025, so an option submitted on 15 November 2025 was within time.

q: Consider the following statements about the full assured payout under UPS: I. It is 50% of the average basic pay of the last 12 months. II. It is payable after 25 years of qualifying service. III. It is payable in full after 10 years of qualifying service. Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: Ten years is the threshold for the minimum payout, not for the full payout. The full rate needs 25 years, so only I and II are correct.

q: What is the rate of the employee contribution under UPS?
e: The employee contributes 10% under UPS, matched by a Government contribution of 10%, with an additional Government pool contribution of 8.5%.

q: Match List I with List II and select the correct answer: I. Date UPS became operational II. Railway Board circular introducing UPS III. Cut-off date for the UPS option IV. Minimum qualifying service for the minimum assured payout a. 30 November 2025 b. 1 April 2025 c. RBE No. 25/2025 d. 10 years
e: UPS became operational on 1 April 2025 vide RBE 25/2025; the option cut-off was 30 November 2025 and the minimum payout needs 10 years of service.

q: The assured payout of a deceased UPS subscriber was Rs 45,000 per month. What monthly family payout is payable under UPS?
e: Family payout under UPS is 60% of the assured payout.

q: Consider the following statements: I. The minimum assured payout under UPS is Rs 10,000 per month. II. The minimum assured payout is admissible after 10 years of qualifying service. III. The family payout under UPS is 50% of the assured payout. Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: The family payout is 60% of the assured payout, not 50%. Statements I and II are correct; III is wrong.

q: Assertion (A): UPS is an option available within the NPS framework. Reason (R): UPS was made operational from 1 April 2025 as an assured-payout option inside the NPS architecture.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
options.C: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
options.D: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true

e: Both statements are true, and the Reason states exactly why the Assertion holds: UPS sits inside NPS as its assured-payout option.

q: A clerk advises a 2012 appointee that by opting for UPS he will automatically return to the Old Pension Scheme and also resume subscription to SRPF. What is the correct advice?

options.A: The clerk is right on both counts
options.B: He will return to the Old Pension Scheme but not to SRPF
options.C: He will do neither; UPS is only an assured-payout option inside NPS and revives neither OPS nor SRPF
options.D: He will resume SRPF subscription but stay outside OPS

e: UPS changes the pension promise for NPS-covered staff; it restores neither the Old Pension Scheme nor SRPF/GPF subscription.

q: Consider the following statements about migration to UPS: I. The cut-off date for exercising the option was 30 November 2025. II. A subscriber who retired on or after 1 April 2025 and has already availed NPS benefits cannot migrate to UPS. III. A subscriber who has already availed NPS benefits after such retirement can migrate to UPS at any later date. Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: Statement III directly contradicts the bar in the clarification reproduced in RBE 48/2026. Only I and II are correct.

q: The basic pay of a UPS subscriber taken for contribution purposes is Rs 90,000 per month. What is the monthly Government pool contribution alone?
e: The Government pool contribution is 8.5%, separate from the 10% matching contribution.

q: UPS was introduced on the Railways vide which Railway Board circular?
e: UPS was introduced vide RBE No. 25/2025 and became operational from 1 April 2025. RBE 48/2026 is a later clarification on migration.

q: Consider the following statements about the nature of UPS: I. UPS is an assured-payout option for NPS-covered employees. II. UPS does not restore the Old Pension Scheme. III. UPS revives subscription to SRPF for post-2004 appointees. Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: UPS neither restores OPS nor revives SRPF. It is an option inside NPS, so only I and II are correct.

q: Which one of the following statements about UPS dates and minimum benefits is NOT correct?

options.A: The cut-off date for exercising the UPS option was 31 March 2026
options.C: The minimum assured payout is Rs 10,000 per month after 10 years
options.D: The family payout is 60% of the assured payout

e: The cut-off was 30 November 2025, not 31 March 2026. The other three statements are correct.

q: Assertion (A): The family payout under UPS is 60% of the assured payout. Reason (R): The employee contribution under UPS is 10%.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
options.C: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
options.D: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true

e: Both facts are true, but the employee contribution rate does not explain the family payout percentage, so the Reason does not explain the Assertion.

q: A UPS subscriber has an average basic pay of Rs 75,000 for the last 12 months and 20 years of qualifying service. Taking the assured payout proportionately for service short of 25 years, what is his monthly assured payout?
e: The full rate for 25 years would be 50% of Rs 75,000; for 20 years it is taken proportionately as 20/25 of that rate.

q: A UPS subscriber retires with only 9 years of qualifying service and claims the minimum assured payout of Rs 10,000 per month on that basis. What is the correct position?

options.A: He gets half the minimum payout for 9 years of service
options.B: He gets the full payout because 9 years is close to 10 years
options.C: The minimum assured payout is not admissible, as it requires at least 10 years of qualifying service
options.D: The claim is admissible because any service earns the minimum payout

e: The Rs 10,000 minimum is linked to completion of 10 years of qualifying service; 9 years does not meet that threshold.

q: Consider the following statements about Government support under UPS: I. The Government matching contribution is 10%. II. The Government pool contribution is 8.5%. III. Taken together, the Government contribution works out to 18.5%. Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: All three are correct: 10% matching plus 8.5% pool contribution totals 18.5% from the Government side.

q: Consider the following statements about the basis of the UPS assured payout: I. It is worked out on the average basic pay of the last 12 months. II. It is worked out on the basic pay drawn in the last month of service alone. III. It is worked out on the average of basic pay plus dearness allowance of the last 12 months. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: The UPS formula uses the average basic pay of the last 12 months. Neither the last month alone nor a basic-plus-DA average is the stated basis.

q: Assertion (A): UPS restores the Old Pension Scheme for all railway employees. Reason (R): UPS operates as an option inside the NPS architecture.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
options.C: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
options.D: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true

e: UPS does not restore OPS, so the Assertion is false. The Reason is true: UPS sits inside the NPS architecture.

q: A subscriber has 10 years of qualifying service and an average basic pay of Rs 40,000 for the last 12 months. His proportionate payout works out below the floor. What monthly assured payout will he actually get under UPS?
e: The proportionate figure is Rs 8,000, but with 10 years of service the minimum assured payout of Rs 10,000 applies.

q: What is the rate of the Government pool contribution under UPS?
e: Over and above its 10% matching contribution, the Government makes a pool contribution of 8.5% under UPS.

q: Consider the following statements: I. NPS-covered serving employees could exercise the option for UPS. II. Employees already covered by the Old Pension Scheme were required to shift compulsorily to UPS. III. The option was to be exercised by the cut-off date of 30 November 2025. Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: UPS is an option for NPS-covered staff, to be exercised by the cut-off; there was no compulsory shifting of OPS-covered employees. Only I and III are correct.

q: A subscriber completes 25 years of qualifying service and asks on what basis his full assured payout will be fixed. What should he be told?

options.A: It will be a flat Rs 10,000 per month for every subscriber
options.B: It will be 50% of the average basic pay of his last 12 months
options.C: It will depend entirely on market returns on his NPS corpus
options.D: It will be 60% of his last drawn basic pay

e: On completion of 25 years, the full assured payout is 50% of the average basic pay of the last 12 months.

q: Assertion (A): The total Government contribution under UPS is higher than the employee contribution. Reason (R): The Government pays a matching contribution of 10% and a pool contribution of 8.5%, while the employee pays 10%.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
options.C: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
options.D: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true

e: Both are true: Government pays 18.5% against the employee's 10%, and the Reason gives exactly the break-up that explains the Assertion.

q: Consider the following statements about family payout under UPS: I. Family payout is 60% of the assured payout. II. Family payout is equal to the full assured payout of the subscriber. III. Family payout is 50% of the assured payout. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
e: Only statement I is correct. The family payout is fixed at 60% of the assured payout, neither the full amount nor 50%.

q: A UPS subscriber completes 25 years of qualifying service with an average basic pay of Rs 64,000 for the last 12 months. On his death after retirement, what monthly family payout will be payable?
e: His assured payout is 50% of Rs 64,000, i.e. Rs 32,000, and the family payout is 60% of that amount.

q: Match List I with List II and select the correct answer: I. Rate of full assured payout II. Qualifying service for full assured payout III. Qualifying service for minimum assured payout IV. Amount of minimum assured payout a. Rs 10,000 per month b. 25 years c. 50% of average basic pay of last 12 months d. 10 years
e: Full payout is 50% of average basic pay after 25 years; the minimum of Rs 10,000 per month applies after 10 years.

q: Consider the following statements: I. Full assured payout under UPS requires 25 years of qualifying service. II. The minimum assured payout under UPS requires 10 years of qualifying service. III. A subscriber with 10 years of service gets the full 50% payout rate without reduction. Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: Ten years earns only the minimum/proportionate position, not the full rate. Statements I and II are correct; III is wrong.

q: A UPS subscriber dies while receiving an assured payout. His widow asks how her monthly payment will be determined. What is the correct reply?

options.A: It will be 60% of the assured payout that was payable to the subscriber
options.B: It will be equal to his full assured payout
options.C: It will be 10% of his last basic pay
options.D: It will be a flat Rs 10,000 in every case

e: Family payout under UPS is fixed at 60% of the assured payout, whatever that payout was.

q: Assertion (A): A subscriber who retired on or after 1 April 2025 and has already availed NPS benefits cannot migrate to UPS. Reason (R): Such a subscriber remains free to migrate to UPS even after availing NPS benefits.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
options.C: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
options.D: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true

e: The Assertion states the bar in the clarification reproduced in RBE 48/2026. The Reason states the opposite and is therefore false.

q: The basic pay of a UPS subscriber taken for contribution purposes is Rs 50,000 per month. What is the total monthly amount credited from all contributions — employee, Government matching and Government pool taken together?
e: The three contributions total 10% + 10% + 8.5% = 28.5% of Rs 50,000.

q: Consider the following statements about contributions under UPS: I. The Government matching contribution is 10%. II. The Government pool contribution is 8.5%. III. The Government makes no contribution of any kind under UPS. Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: The Government contributes both by matching (10%) and through the pool (8.5%), so statement III is false. Only I and II are correct.

q: UPS is an assured-payout option available within which pension framework?
e: UPS sits inside the NPS architecture as its assured-payout option; it is not part of OPS, SRPF or GPF.

q: Which one of the following statements about UPS payout rates and contributions is NOT correct?

options.A: The Government matching contribution under UPS is 10%
options.B: The full assured payout under UPS is 60% of the average basic pay of the last 12 months
options.C: The minimum assured payout is admissible after 10 years of qualifying service
options.D: UPS is an option within the NPS architecture

e: The full assured payout is 50%, not 60%, of the average basic pay of the last 12 months. The 60% figure is the family payout share.

q: Consider the following statements: I. UPS became operational from 1 April 2025. II. RBE No. 25/2025 is the Railway Board circular associated with the introduction of UPS. III. The cut-off date for the UPS option was 1 April 2025. Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: 1 April 2025 is the operational date, not the cut-off; the cut-off was 30 November 2025. Only I and II are correct.

q: A UPS subscriber has basic pay of Rs 60,000 and Dearness Allowance of Rs 36,000. The total Government contribution credited for him in a month, taking the matching contribution and the additional pool contribution together, is:
e: Under UPS the Government contributes a matching 10% plus an additional pool contribution of 8.5% on (basic pay + DA) of Rs 96,000, i.e. 18.5% in all, which works out to Rs 17,760 a month.

q: An employee appointed in 2012, who is covered by NPS, asks whether the UPS option concerns him at all, or whether he should instead apply to join SRPF. What is the correct reply?

options.A: UPS does not concern him; he should join SRPF
options.B: He can join both UPS and SRPF together
options.C: UPS is meant for NPS-covered staff like him; it does not open SRPF membership to him
options.D: He must first shift to the Old Pension Scheme to consider UPS

e: Post-2004 appointees are in NPS and cannot join SRPF. UPS is precisely the assured-payout option created for NPS-covered staff.

q: Assertion (A): The cut-off date for exercising the UPS option was 30 November 2025. Reason (R): Full assured payout under UPS requires 25 years of qualifying service.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
options.C: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
options.D: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true

e: Both statements are true, but the service condition for full payout does not explain the option cut-off date, so the Reason does not explain the Assertion.

q: Consider the following statements: I. UPS provides an assured payout to optees who fulfil its conditions. II. Under pure NPS, the pension outcome depends on the accumulated corpus and annuity, with no UPS-type assured payout. III. UPS abolishes NPS altogether for every railway employee. Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: UPS works inside NPS and does not abolish it. Statements I and II are correct; III is wrong.

q: A deceased UPS subscriber was receiving only the minimum assured payout of Rs 10,000 per month. What monthly family payout is payable under UPS?
e: Family payout is 60% of the assured payout, applied here to the minimum payout of Rs 10,000.

q: What is the minimum assured monthly payout under UPS, and after how much qualifying service is it admissible?
e: The floor under UPS is Rs 10,000 per month, admissible after 10 years of qualifying service; the full 50% rate needs 25 years.

q: An NPS-covered employee submits his UPS option on 15 December 2025 and insists that the date does not matter because UPS has no closing date for options. What is the correct position?

options.A: He is right; options can be filed on any date
options.B: His option is in time because December 2025 is within the same financial year
options.C: He can be taken into UPS only through the Old Pension Scheme route
options.D: His option is beyond the prescribed cut-off of 30 November 2025 and cannot be treated as exercised within the window

e: The option window closed on 30 November 2025. An option dated 15 December 2025 falls outside that prescribed window.
